name: Axicabtagene ciloleucel
drug_class: CD19-directed autologous CAR T-cell therapy (CD28 costimulation)
route_note: Single IV infusion of modified autologous T cells after fludarabine–cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion
originator: Kite Pharma, licensed from the US National Cancer Institute (Steven Rosenberg, James Kochenderfer)

discovery.by: Steven Rosenberg and James Kochenderfer (National Cancer Institute)
discovery.note: Retroviral CAR with the FMC63 anti-CD19 scFv, a CD28 costimulatory domain and CD3ζ.

tagline: CD19 CAR T therapy that became second-line standard for large B-cell lymphoma
summary: Axicabtagene ciloleucel is an autologous CAR T-cell therapy targeting CD19, built on a CD28 costimulatory design developed at the US National Cancer Institute. It is approved for large B-cell lymphoma, including as second-line treatment, and for follicular lymphoma.
mechanism: Patient T cells are transduced with a gamma-retroviral vector encoding an anti-CD19 CAR with CD28 and CD3ζ signalling domains.

After infusion, the CAR T cells expand rapidly, recognise CD19 on lymphoma cells and kill them. The CD28 domain drives fast, intense expansion, associated with high response rates but frequent neurotoxicity and cytokine release syndrome.
uses: Large B-cell lymphoma refractory to or relapsing within 12 months of first-line chemoimmunotherapy
Relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma after two or more lines
Relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more lines

history.title: First CD19 CAR response
history.detail: NCI reports regression of lymphoma in a patient treated with anti-CD19 CAR T cells.

history.title: ZUMA-1 and approval
history.detail: FDA approves Yescarta in October for refractory large B-cell lymphoma.

history.title: Gilead acquires Kite
history.detail: Gilead buys Kite Pharma for about $11.9 billion.

history.title: Follicular lymphoma
history.detail: Accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma (ZUMA-5).

history.title: Second-line approval
history.detail: ZUMA-7 shows superiority over standard salvage chemotherapy and transplant; FDA approves second-line use.

history.title: Survival benefit
history.detail: ZUMA-7 reports improved overall survival, the first for a CAR T therapy in a randomised trial versus standard care.

history.title: T-cell malignancy warning
history.detail: A class boxed warning on secondary T-cell malignancies is added.

pk.half_life: CAR transgene peaks within ~2 weeks and declines over months
pk.metabolism: In vivo expansion and contraction of cells

safety.boxed_warning: Cytokine release syndrome, neurological toxicities and T-cell malignancies; available only at certified treatment centres.

facts: The CD28-based CAR design originated in the laboratory of Steven Rosenberg at the US National Cancer Institute.
Its 2022 approval moved CAR T-cell therapy ahead of autologous stem-cell transplant for early-relapsing large B-cell lymphoma.
